review_title: Neato D7 Connected: Great when new, watch out for wear items.
review_text:
Neato D7 Connected

Update 7/31/202
I purchased two wheel/motor units off ebay (not from the "official" source). these are probably parted out from otherwise dead units, but they were cheaper than the new pieces by enough to try.
Replacing the wheel assemblies requires removing around 12 screws, detaching 7 or 8 wiring connectors and basically disassembling the entire machine.
The Neato units are definitely not repair friendly, especially for a part that I would consider as a normal wear item.
There doesn't seem to be any official instructions on how to take your D7 apart, so search on the internet and do your best.
By contrast, iRobot has instructions on their support site on how to replace the wheel modules, and it's a lot simpler.
If my D7 decides to need more parts, I'm sending it off to the Goodwill and buying a Roomba.
Rating revised downward.

Bought this to replace a Eufy model that makes replacing the battery a chore (including soldering a new battery in), so I made sure that the battery for the replacement was, well, replaceable. I was also looking for a vacuum robot that used a good pattern rather than the random pattern that the Eufy used. The D7 seemed to tick the boxes and got good reviews for actual cleaning. There are, however some issues. It likes to climb some objects and then gets a bit stuck on them, and rather than call for help, it keeps grinding away trying to continue its work. This grinds down the rubber on the wheels and leaves marks on whatever it has climbed on. The wheels are held on by screws, which seem to loosen over time and then let the internal gears skip and wear.

Good:
-Cleans well, or at least there's almost always a bin full to empty after it cleans the house.
-Decent navigation, can see that it cleans in a rational pattern, rather than random like the old Eufy that I had previously which seemed to be completely random.
-User replaceable battery (Something that was lacking on the Eufy model I had)

Bad:
-Small bin. Needs emptying daily.
-Loud, even on Eco mode
-Loud gear grinding noises.
-Keeps banging into things, repeatedly.
-Gets stuck and grinds away at the base of one chair in particular that consists of 3/4" high wooden pieces. Discolored the wood edges and wears down the rubber on the wheels. I resorted to putting bumpers on the front of the Neato to try to prevent it from climbing up onto the wood. This sometimes works, but Neato has a propensity for reversing onto things.
-Wheels unscrew themselves, leading to looseness and wobble, and then gear grinding and failure. Needs a Torx bit to tighten the wheel.
-Wheel assembly from Neato's recommended vendor on Amazon costs $92.50 per side. That's much higher than it ought to be, and a reason to look at how much other botvac companies charge for wear item service parts. (hint: Roomba wheel assemblies are ~$32)

Would I buy another? Probably not, knowing what I do now. The D7 got great reviews, and does seem to clean well, but primarily the replacement parts cost (wheel assemblies) makes it problematic in the long term. Now my decision is if it is worth it to spend close to $200 (about half of what I paid for the whole D7) to replace the wheel assemblies, which I now know are a wear item, or spend more on a completely new, but different brand of vacuum.

review_text: [[VIDEOID:1d7e6bf0d604b77d53f20947ab3e212f]] This thing is great. To start off with, we have a family of 7, plus two dogs and a cat.  Most of our floors are hard. I wanted something that can pick up the fur and keep the floors clean. This does the job. It's quiet and runs for a couple of hours. The reason for four stars instead of five is a couple of reasons: Every once in a while, it loses its mind. It'll get stuck in a corner and have trouble finding its way out—even though there's a clear way out (see the video).  It'll burn its whole battery and not clean. We'll let it charge and then run it again and everything seems to work fine, then. Also, I wish it had a bigger rubber bumper on the front sensor (maybe even one above the sensor and not just below). As the Deebot edges, the sensor gets scratched. After a few months, the Deebot runs into everything instead of sensing the object. I ended up putting Gorilla Tape over the sensor. Once that gets scratched, I just replace the tape.
